name: Power Generation & Grid Node

placement_rationale.text: 250 km sits in the strategic_rear band, mirroring the side_a power-plant node for a symmetric picture of deep-strike reach on both sides, per this asset's own employment_notes. This extends past doctrine.md §2's explicitly quantified 'medium/long-range strike & recon: 10–150+ km' layer, whose '+' marks exactly this kind of deeper reach, consistent with both sides fielding cruise missiles and one-way-attack drones capable of reaching well past 150 km. As a representative composite node (not a named facility, per its own sources) rather than a specific documented location, deep-rear siting is the doctrinally correct default for the category.

sources.label: Composite/illustrative — no single named facility; category per master prompt asset list

representative_system: Composite — a generic thermal/hydro generation plant and grid substation, not a named facility

cost.display: Not a procured unit — infrastructure whose value is measured in grid capacity and repair cost after a strike, not a purchase price

key_facts.label: Why it matters
key_facts.value: One node can cascade outages across a wide grid area

key_facts.label: Defended by
key_facts.value: Layered short/point air defense rather than any organic defense

key_facts.label: Repair tempo
key_facts.value: Repeated strikes outpace repair during sustained campaigns

short_role: Representative strategic-rear infrastructure target — mirrors the equivalent node on the other side for a symmetric picture of what deep-strike systems on both sides can reach.
characteristics: A single generation or transformer node failure can cascade into outages well beyond the immediate facility
Has no offensive capability of its own — its only 'connection' to the fight is being defended and repaired
Sits at strategic-rear depth, within reach of deep-strike drones and cruise missiles on both sides
employment_notes: Exists on the map to represent the category the master brief calls out explicitly — strategic/operational/tactical targets at varying depth — mirrored on this side for symmetry with the equivalent node on the other.
contrast_vs_traditional: Strategic infrastructure has always been a wartime target; what changed is the volume and reach of what can now attack it, and the corresponding reach of point-defense systems now dedicated to protecting fixed civilian-facing infrastructure rather than only military positions.
